chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: Helen Humes arrives; Hazel Scott and Rose Murphy at the Famous Door
summary: After Billie stayed nearly a year, Helen Humes joined in July 1938, while Jones brought Hazel Scott in as intermission pianist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: And then we came back for 2 months at the place. Like he said, you used - see, we just got with the right people to make the right things. But who was the coordinator -
How long did Billie stay in your band, Basie's band?
Did you use another girl vocalist after her?

After her Buck Clayton had 25 girls and I had 25 girls to see who was going to come in Basie's band. Who came in the band? Helen Humes, 1938, July. When we opened there we were supposed to have Rose Murphy play intermission piano, and Hazel Scott was down the street at the Hickory House on a bicycle with bobby socks on. I went down the street and got Hazel Scott coming in with a skirt and a whosis to come in and sit and Walter Page and myself played with Hazel Scott.
What's a whosis, Jo? We got to explain that to the people.

She had on a skirt, a blouse, and had on the bobby socks - the loafers and the little white socks, and she had a bicycle. I made her bring the bicycle because Kelly's Stable had just moved across the street from there. Ralph Watkins had that, you know.
Across the street on 52nd Street. It moved to the north side of the street.
I said, 'Come down, 'cause Rose Murphy is ill and she won't be able to show up.' So Rose Murphy came in and after Rose Murphy we had Gladys Palmer as intermission pianist, in 1938.
